posts.text: Around 14–15 million years ago, during a cool, arid period, forests in Northwest Africa turned into C3 grasslands, according to a study of plant waxes. The modern savanna, dominated by grasses using the C4 photosystem, appeared in the late Miocene. In PNAS: https://ow.ly/ATpF50ZzW7t

Rapid and prolonged greenhouse warming during the Paleocene–Eocene Thermal Maximum caused forests to thin, drastically reshaped plant communities, and reduced overall vegetation carbon storage. 

The results in Science could foreshadow challenges facing modern forests. https://scim.ag/4g8uUST

posts.text: Conodont fossils contain data on the Kasimovian–Gzhelian Thermal Maximum, a global temperature rise of about 7.5 °C some 304 million years ago. The event was likely triggered by a modest carbon release that crossed a tipping point. In PNAS: https://ow.ly/wUOE50ZzttA

Exclusive: For decades, researchers have marveled at how this open-air art gallery resisted extreme weathering. The secret may be macabre.
